gt_definition.phase_order: QS -> GI -> SSSW -> SLT -> SSLW -> GT
gt_definition.start: the accepted terminal load-peak boundary at the end of SSLW; in a bilateral mismatch, GT can be extended to a later cadence-consistent peak with strong FMG support
gt_definition.end: the final available sample of the trigger-paired recording window
gt_definition.meaning: terminal stopping/ending region, retaining settling or subsequent postural movement
gt_definition.status: model-assisted provisional; the start boundary is an operational stopping-region estimate, not proof that gait ended precisely there

candidate_landmark_audit.meaning: Any remaining candidate peaks are not a GT cycle structure; GT explicitly retains terminal settling or postural movement.

cycle_grouping.stored_structure: one continuous terminal GT region per physical window, copied to left and right limb-specific traces
cycle_grouping.reason: GT is a terminal stopping/ending region rather than a stored walking-cycle series. It has no five-repetition identities or valid per-cycle subdivisions.
